create_display_works.ponder.flip_dot_dri: Building and powering a Flip-Dot Display
Each block has 8 by 8 dots. Place matching faces together to build one seamless canvas.
Drive the built-in cogs from the side. Rotation passes between adjacent displays.
Faster rotation means faster diagonal flips. Changed discs start together and can reverse immediately when new information arrives.
Stopping the drive finishes the current flips, then holds. Video pauses; new information waits until power returns.
create_display_works.ponder.flip_dot_inf: Select this display with a Display Link, then place the link on a source such as a Stockpile Switch. Select the target row in the link interface.
A renamed Name Tag writes one row. A Create Clipboard writes several rows. Right-click with an empty hand to open media controls.
Dye changes the front color across the whole board. Applying either existing color swaps front and back. Apply a new dye twice to make it the back color.

create_display_works.ponder.flip_dot_med: Right-click with an empty hand. Enter a media URL, public YouTube video or local file, import a preview, then apply it.
Import images or silent animations up to 100 MB and 60 seconds at 10 FPS. Choose stretch, fit or fill; adjust threshold, inversion and dithering.
Dot frames are saved in the world. Slow cogs may not finish each flip before the next frame arrives. New Display Link input replaces media playback.
For hand-drawn symbols, start a Clipboard page with [pixels]. Add rows using # for light dots and periods or spaces for dark dots.
